dependency.note: Grade 1 proposal including lead-reviewed age-context deferral; this is not an accepted main or deployment receipt.

interpretation: Semantic judgments are not learner mastery, proof of delivery or consumer selection certification. Candidate/prerequisite references are not authored direct links. Partial conditions and quality notes do not authorize new topics or changes to existing claims.

expectations.rationale: Generic process operations exist; integrated performance, safety equipment and reporting conditions remain explicit.
remainingConditions: Overall coverage is reviewed independently, not automatically certified by counting child associations.

expectations.rationale: Question selection, close observation, shared fact gathering and evidence-based reporting have existing claims.
remainingConditions: Check an integrated research performance in the science strands; the collection of generic claims is not a completed investigation. Process guidance is flexible by readiness, not a requirement for advanced bibliography or bias analysis in Grade 2.

expectations.rationale: Existing claims cover guided experiments, predictions, recording and conclusions without importing later formal hypothesis/variable terminology.
remainingConditions: A safe, connected performance in relevant science content remains to be demonstrated.

expectations.rationale: Sketches, safe making, motion-design testing and comparisons supply existing engineering operations appropriate to the Grade 2 body content.
remainingConditions: Assess a coherent design/build/test performance, its evidence and response to results; isolated operations are insufficient.
Use readiness-dependent process guidance without requiring every advanced engineering step.

expectations.rationale: The safety and early making claims include hazard-aware plans, safe sensory exploration, careful equipment use and cleanup.
remainingConditions: Explicitly check task-appropriate protective clothing/equipment in addition to general safe handling. Later drilling-specific safeguards do not supply a universal early investigation claim.

expectations.rationale: Scientific reporting and existing vocabulary/audience decisions are reusable.
remainingConditions: Check the actual scientific vocabulary and audience/format choices in a science report; generic vocabulary or writing-process success alone does not certify the integrated requirement.

expectations.rationale: Science application/decomposition and impact explanations remain to be demonstrated.

expectations.rationale: Planning a Task explicitly breaks a larger task into smaller ordered steps. The algorithm and first-program claims support implementing and running the plan; no new decomposition topic is needed.
remainingConditions: Require learner-authored decomposition and a science investigation/model, rather than only running a supplied sequence or unrelated maths animation.

expectations.rationale: Everyday AI examples include benefits and limitations, providing a direct emerging-technology contribution.
remainingConditions: Explain an effect of programmed behaviour as well as an emerging-technology example; device naming alone is insufficient.

deferredCandidates.reason: Broader historical effects can support discussion, but do not themselves explain the role of a programmed instruction.

expectations.rationale: Practical material/design applications have support; integrated tasks and community contribution resources remain.
remainingConditions: Overall coverage is reviewed independently, not automatically certified by counting child associations.

expectations.rationale: Purposeful products and places, together with property-to-function explanations, support familiar scientific/design applications. Use a relevant example such as a spill-resistant container and its material choice, not an unrelated device list.
Motion-design testing supplies science/data work and shared research supplies information gathering and writing.
remainingConditions: Assess the integrated use of another subject in a real problem; co-listing generic skills is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: Existing biography, community-history and ecological-knowledge claims provide candidates; the resource task does not justify separate community clones.
remainingConditions: Verify age-appropriate resources from multiple communities and examine what the contributions changed.
Do not treat a single biography or a generic ecological statement as complete evidence.

deferredCandidates.reason: One scientific biography is a possible example, not a multi-community review.
Requires factual/cultural and whole-claim review before contextual reuse.
Investigating the importance of a local person or group can support the process, but scientific contributions and multiple communities need verified content.

expectations.rationale: Human-impact practices have direct support; animal-driven negative effects/mitigation remain.
remainingConditions: Overall coverage is reviewed independently, not automatically certified by counting child associations.

expectations.rationale: Organism-driven habitat change and pollination provide actual animal effects, including practical consequences for food production.
remainingConditions: Assess a negative animal-impact case and a justified mitigation. A beneficial pollination example or habitat-change description alone does not cover this.

expectations.rationale: The existing impact claim identifies multiple kinds of environmental harm, proposes responses and explains their benefits. Select cases affecting animals and their habitats rather than certifying all source requirements from one slogan.
Movement and selected adaptation cases have support; constant/changing traits and complete life-history comparison sets remain.
remainingConditions: Overall coverage is reviewed independently, not automatically certified by counting child associations.

expectations.rationale: Animal-group comparisons and observed growth provide distinct pieces of physical comparison.
remainingConditions: Explicitly compare stable and changing features using appropriate cases; a list of group features or the statement that babies grow is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: The minibeast movement claim describes and matches several movement forms across different animals. The source does not mandate every locomotion form or a particular vertebrate group, so a new broad animal-movement clone is unnecessary.
Diverse life-cycle models and bird/mammal juvenile-to-adult examples are present in existing claims.
remainingConditions: Check complete cases across all four required groups. A two-organism minimum and juvenile/adult matching alone do not prove the whole required case set; do not add group-specific clones to repair the assessment sample.

expectations.rationale: General cycle comparisons and insect transformation include body changes and stage-related feeding/growth roles.
remainingConditions: Compare appearance and behaviour through complete cases for varied animals; naming stages or explaining only a larva is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: The camouflage claim explains multiple examples and their protective or feeding purpose. Physical adaptations are sufficient under the source wording; behavioural examples or later evolutionary theory are not extra mandatory clauses.
Household material practices and consequences require actual source-specific assessments.
remainingConditions: Overall coverage is reviewed independently, not automatically certified by counting child associations.

expectations.rationale: Food handling/storage and hazard-aware substance handling supply safety components without inventing another general safety claim.
remainingConditions: Evaluate an actual set of household use/storage/disposal practices and their environmental consequences, then explain improvements. A food-hygiene or equipment-safety routine alone does not cover all of that.

expectations.rationale: Existing state-change knowledge can support this application; it is not itself an evaluated consequence.
remainingConditions: Use verified cases and explain effects on people and environments. Do not attach every phase-change topic to the impact requirement merely because it mentions melting.

expectations.rationale: Several classification/transition claims have support; stable-state cases, mixtures and symbol meanings retain conditions.
remainingConditions: Overall coverage is reviewed independently, not automatically certified by counting child associations.

remainingConditions: Check non-transition cases and material-specific conditions too; warming something does not automatically change its state.

remainingConditions: Use and explain actual liquid/solid combinations with a purpose. Following a solid-only snack recipe or merely saying mixture is insufficient.

expectations.rationale: Classifying Materials explicitly plans property tests, records results and groups them; its assessment includes float tests. Material Properties includes absorbency/waterproofness. Together they support the two classifications without adding a buoyant-force theory topic.
remainingConditions: Use both property dimensions in the selected test set; full topic mastery is not inferred from one floating object.

expectations.rationale: The Personal and Social Development health/safety-sign claim already includes poison/hazard symbols on household products. This is a direct reuse across subjects.
remainingConditions: Check multiple applicable substance symbols and explain the represented hazards using an accurate resource; a generic tell-an-adult response alone is not the complete meaning requirement.

expectations.rationale: Mechanism-linked social/environmental cases remain unverified.

expectations.rationale: The historical technology claim includes cart/transport and household-work comparisons, which can supply concrete impact examples.
remainingConditions: Connect the selected tool to its simple-machine function and compare relevant community cases; a general modern-versus-old story is insufficient.

deferredCandidates.reason: Direct lever/pulley knowledge exists, but the complete later-start claim also requires gear-force explanations; local age fit is not inferred from one matching case.

expectations.rationale: Generic environmental reasoning and tool-purpose knowledge provide background, not a demonstrated mechanism-linked assessment.
remainingConditions: Identify the mechanism in a movement technology and evaluate its effects using a supported case. Do not manufacture a direct link from a generic pollution answer.

expectations.rationale: Motion/repositioning have direct support; complete machine categories/functions and with/without force comparisons remain.

expectations.rationale: The existing movement claim explicitly distinguishes rolling, sliding, bouncing and spinning and gives contrasting cases. No new list of movements is needed.
Existing pushes/pulls evidence covers movement and changes arising from different directions and strengths; it supports more than one way to reposition an object without introducing formal mechanics.
Lever/pulley concepts and ramp examples exist, but the complete named set has not been found in assessed evidence across subjects.
remainingConditions: Account explicitly for every required category. A ramp example is not proof that the full category set is named or distinguished. No new topics are approved by this finding.

expectations.rationale: Comparing stronger/weaker pushes supplies relevant qualitative force reasoning.
